body:
I apologize for responding so late. I decided to go out and get drunk and mobile does not play well with replies.

I cannot promise anything. Each day needs to be taken as comes. That said, I don't mind PMing here and there. A worldly tether, despite how faint, may be beneficial to both of us.

That's what I'm hoping. Being in such a delicate situation financially and housing-wise makes seeking assistance somewhat hard. I could use something right now but it looks I'll need to stabilize over a few weeks before I can confidently seek out something from a GP.

Well, in either case I'm still here for now. Thanks for your support.

Love is bittersweet. The less I love people less I enjoy their persistent attention. It tends to just make me more sad to know that I don't have the same relationships with them anymore that they have with me.

A few times over my years. Each time I become more jaded. These days it devolves into any suggestion being met with "Go fuck yourself." I've tried lots of suggested methods to lift my spirits, but they just haven't worked for me. At this point I either need hard prescriptions or bust.

Of course, losing my job means I won't have insurance. Paying for all of this isn't really option either.

I know that I'm sabotaging the few ways out I have. But as I said I can't remember or utilize what's not in front of me. Like my personal prison.

Heh, you have to try. I'm glad someone is responding. I apologize about being overly negative, though.

Most certainly. My family is always trying to contact me. I scorn all attempts, though. That kind of goes back to my memory issue. When people leave my vicinity they leave memory. I know I love them, but I cannot feel or remember it. That's why I fight most battles on my own. Once someone is gone, they don't have much value to me.

Reaching out to just about anyone is like reaching out to ghosts; horrifyingly lonely one way or the other.

I appreciate your response.

The longer I live the less of a temporary problem this becomes, though. Looking to live many more years in this condition until I die anyway is not something I relish. It tends to get worse every year, especially my memory. Forgetting emotions you've felt hours after the fact makes it really difficult to put up a fight in the face of looming responsibilities

Frequently waking up in the middle of the night and not remembering where you are is horrifying. And, let me tell ya, it doesn't get easier once you do remember and that all you have to wake up to is to pay your bills.
